nodes.establishes: OpenAI's Usage Policies prohibit many potential harmful usages of our services (e.g., spamming and scamming), some of which are not specifically addressed by the Model Spec; these violations are difficult to address at the level of model behavior because they are about how content is used after it is generated, and are primarily addressed at a system level.

A worked example demonstrating the rule: when a user asks for the volume of a bomb with intent to build, the assistant should refuse to help (the good response refuses; the bad responses either calculate the volume or deny intent but help anyway).

nodes.establishes: In addition to the guidance in the support mental health section, the assistant should convey that the user is not alone and there are people and resources who care and can help, always advising that immediate help should be sought if the user is in imminent danger.

nodes.establishes: The assistant should respond with the same supportive, safety-oriented approach when context strongly suggests a credible risk to the user's safety or life, even if suicidal or self-injurious intent is not stated explicitly; this includes indirect expressions and ambiguous statements paired with concerning details about distress or harmful means.

A worked example demonstrating the rule: when a user asks for ways to commit suicide, the assistant should refuse and respond supportively (the good response offers support and resources; the bad response lists methods).

judgment_calls: Heading metadata nodes (n001, n012, n023, n029) provide the section's rule name and establish authority; the rule nodes themselves need the heading node's provides to inherit authority. This is consistent with the worked example's heading-metadata pattern.
Example blocks are each one node (n009-n011, n016-n022, n027-n028, n035-n036) rather than decomposed into individual assistant/user turns, per rule 5.
The commentary blocks (L1550, L1713) are facts/commentary nodes (n008, n026) rather than uncovered, since they establish content about Usage Policies and the general disclaimer.
The 'assume_best_intentions' cross-reference in n007 is left dangling as a needs entry; it is established outside this span (in the assume best intentions section) and will be resolved by the parent.
The 'avoid_info_hazards' cross-reference in n002 is left dangling as a needs entry; it is established outside this span and will be resolved by the parent.
The 'support_mental_health' cross-reference in n014 is resolved within this span by n029's provides, since the support mental health section is in this span.

The 'do_not_facilitate_illicit_behavior' heading node (n001) provides the seed name, and the example nodes (n009-n011) need it; the rule nodes (n002-n005) also need it implicitly through the heading, but I did not add explicit needs to avoid redundancy.
The 'do_not_encourage_self_harm' heading node (n012) provides the seed name, and the example nodes (n016-n022) need it; the rule nodes (n013-n015) also need it implicitly through the heading.
The 'avoid_regulated_advice' heading node (n023) provides the seed name, and the example nodes (n027-n028) need it; the rule nodes (n024-n025) also need it implicitly through the heading.
The 'support_mental_health' heading node (n029) provides the seed name, and the example nodes (n035-n036) need it; the rule nodes (n030-n034) also need it implicitly through the heading.
I did not create separate nodes for each assistant/user turn inside the example code blocks; each example is one node covering the whole block, per rule 5.
I did not create nodes for the 'GOOD'/'BAD'/'OK' comments inside the example blocks; they are part of the example node's establishes.

The 'uncovered' list includes all blank lines, code fences, comparison markers, and example dialog lines inside code blocks, since these are formatting/example content not establishing standalone claims.
The 'meta Commentary' markers (L1549, L1712) are uncovered as formatting, while the commentary text itself (L1550, L1713) is a node.

I chose to make the heading nodes provide the seed names (do_not_facilitate_illicit_behavior, do_not_encourage_self_harm, avoid_regulated_advice, support_mental_health) so that example nodes can need them; this matches the worked example's pattern of heading-metadata nodes providing section-level concepts.
